record_body:
Overview
- Large EU-headquartered bank. Mix of consumer + business products.
- Current Redwood usage: Hosted API + Dedicated capacity in eu-west (primary) with us-east as contingency.
- Workloads are sensitive to tail latency and availability during business hours; strict change management.

Primary Workloads / Routes
- /v1/chat/completions: agent assist + contact center summarization (streaming enabled for some apps)
- /v1/embeddings: internal doc search + policy retrieval (bursty batch jobs at top of hour)
- /v1/rerank: used intermittently in search pipeline (not always latency-critical)

Requirements Summary
- Latency/SLO: asked for explicit SLO mapping on “top routes” with tier semantics (they repeatedly cited p95 and p99 behavior during regional pressure).
- Reliability: wants deterministic overload behavior; prefers predictable 429s over elevated 5xx/timeout cascades.
- Routing/fallback: strong preference for no silent quality changes; any fallback must be explicit/allowlisted.
- Compliance: SSO/SAML required; audit logs needed for admin actions + throttling/overload events; data residency in EU for production traffic.

Hot-route capacity protection adoption (notes)
- They were an early driver for clarifying enterprise vs best-effort behavior (noisy neighbor concerns).
- After enablement, they reported improved stability during regional pressure, but saw increased 429s when their client retry logic spiked.
- They requested a temporary burst exception for embeddings batch jobs with guardrails (time-bound + monitored).

Timeline / Activity Log
- 2024-06-18: Account created (initial Dedicated evaluation). Owners: Liam O’Rourke (TAM/owner), Simran Kaur (SE).
- 2024-08: Discovery completed. Security: asked for SOC2 + ISO docs, SAML, audit logs. Noted data residency requirement (EU-only).
- 2025-03: Dedicated capacity started in eu-west. Early success on chat summarization; embeddings pipeline expanded.
- 2025-11-03: Referenced internally as a key impacted customer during fleet-wide latency cascade (see postmortem date; they experienced elevated tail latency on chat route). Customer escalated via Support + CSM.
- 2025-12: Several follow-ups on “noisy neighbor” and predictable overload behavior; pushed for formal tier semantics and per-route budgets.
- 2026-01-15: Escalation check-in call (Fireflies: 2026-01-15-proxima-bank-escalation-checkin-capacity-protection). Customer quote: “We’d rather get a clean 429 than have the whole contact center tool hang.”
- 2026-01-18: Email thread (Gmail: 20260118-enterprise-escalation-overload-protection-exception-request) re: temporary burst allowance for embeddings + request for contractual language clarifying protected route SLOs.
- 2026-01-22: Support ticket SUP-18421: reported 429 spike after priority routing rollout; resolved as expected behavior + client backoff guidance.
- 2026-01-28: Support ticket SUP-18462: streaming client saw inconsistent termination on shed; pointed to fix + docs update.
- 2026-02-07: Latest internal sync: review protection dashboards + confirm canary results stable; next is procurement finalization for expanded Dedicated + compliance add-ons.

Open Questions / To Confirm
- Confirm protected route list for their contract: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings (EU only). Decide whether rerank is “protected” or best-effort.
- Confirm fallback policy guardrails: strict admission control only for chat; embeddings may allow limited fallback to compatible model variant (customer leaning “no” unless explicit).
- Client retry/backoff: request customer to adopt recommended exponential backoff + jitter; align on max concurrency caps to avoid self-induced bursts.

Internal Notes (shorthand)
- Sensitive to change announcements. Prefers “capacity protection” framing vs “priority” language.
- Ask SRE/Platform to share a short, customer-safe explanation of 429 reason codes + what’s overload vs quota.
- Coordinate with Rachel Kim (CSM) for renewal + add-on scope; Simran Kaur (SE) to own technical validation + exception monitoring plan.

Support/Incident Context
- SUP-18433 (latency regression on chat during burst): referenced as motivating pain point; they want ‘enterprise behavior’ guaranteed under pressure.
- Post-rollout: they like improved p99 stability, but want fewer surprises in 429 rates (mostly due to their own scheduled batch patterns).
